review.claim: From How You Pay (button BankPayments.tsx:113, run at :47) the player sets an amount and a day of the month into one of their own open easy-access savings accounts. The command validates the target (own, open, savings, not a term deposit), the amount and the day, records the order in person.payments.standingOrders and schedules bank.standing_order for the next such day at 9 AM. Each month the handler moves the amount from the account it pays from (orderSource: the primary when first read, pinned on a change of primary) into the savings: at once at the same bank, or out on the day and in on the sending bank's days at another bank. It skips the month with 'A Standing Order Didn't Go' when the account is short, closed, dormant, closing, blocked by a switch or a term deposit, then re-arms for the next month. armPayments re-arms orders when a save loads.

review.claim: Breaks a term deposit before its end, at breakQuote's price. The penalty is days of interest by band, capped at the interest earned where the bank caps it, at least a week's interest in the first week, MUFG's early rate, or the interest forfeited as SLATE's estimate. It is free in a grace window or a cooling-off period, and refused where the bank doesn't allow breaking. breakTerm pays principal − (penalty beyond the interest) + kept interest − tax, closes the term and posts an Early Withdrawal Penalty expense. At NatWest it sets breakAt instead, and account_life closes the term when the 35 days' notice runs.

gapsClosed: A current account canceled in its cooling-off was asked only whether anything used it (linkedTo), so one overdrawn closed with its debt, and one with money on its way, card payments pending or savings beside it closed too. It's asked Close It's own refusals (closeRefusal) now.

Your Accounts Over Time offered Cancel It for savings and cards only, so the command's current-account branch had no control. A new current account other than the primary is offered, its Close It refusal said under it with the button grayed out.

A current account canceled in its cooling-off closed with no interest paid and no fees charged, and its overdraft limit left on it, where Close It (closeNow) settles both and the guide said it “closes the same way”. It is settled as Close It settles one now: settleInterest, settleFees, the limit cleared; in Canada the charges for its operation while it was open come back (SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)), where Britain (BCOBS 6.3.2R) and Germany (BGB § 357b(2)) let the bank charge for the service provided. Fees past what it holds with its interest are refused (cancelRefusal), which the panel reads too. Its words on the panel say what comes back.

Canceling kept a savings account’s or term deposit’s interest from it everywhere, and paid a current account’s everywhere. It follows the country’s rule now: kept in Britain and Canada; returned, any already paid posted back with its tax and off the year’s income, in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico.
Canada’s refund of charges covered only a current account; it covers any deposit account now, and Mexico’s with it.
Korea’s deposits had a 14-day cooling-off its rule (금융소비자보호법 제46조) doesn’t give; removed, cards kept.
Close It closed a German account overdrawn by its closing fees; refused now, as Cancel It refuses it.

A term’s interest taken during the term (bank.take_term_interest) went into the primary account, and Cancel It took it back out of there, but cancelRefusal counted only interest paid into the term itself, so nothing refused it and a Commerzbank primary was left at −€6.30 (Postbank −€6.08). interestBackOf now counts each payment by the holder’s account it went into, and cancelRefusal refuses while any of those holds less than goes back out of it. Deutsche Bank’s own terms say only that each side repays what it received within 30 days (its ZinsMarkt Widerrufsfolgen), nothing of keeping it back from the deposit, so it’s refused rather than taken from the term.

Canada’s refund took every bank fee since opening, overdraft interest among them (it’s posted as a bank fee against Overdraft Interest), where SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)(b) refunds charges “other than interest charges”; and it was all credited against Bank Fees. chargesBackOf now leaves out a charge against Overdraft Interest and returns each charge by the expense line it was charged to, which the refund credits.

Canada’s 14 and Mexico’s 10 days were counted as calendar days; their rules count business days (SOR/2021-181 s.5(1); LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1, “diez días hábiles”). coolingOffEnds counts them with afterBusinessDays in the bank’s country and the holder’s region; inCoolingOff and the panel’s “until” date read it (the panel had used the panel bank’s country’s days).

A Canadian card had a 14-day cooling-off. Bank Act s.627.11 lets a credit card agreement be canceled “in accordance with any prescribed requirements”, and SOR/2021-181 prescribes them for a retail deposit account (s.5), a deposit-type instrument (s.6) and the products s.4 lists, no card among them (read 2026-10-15). inCoolingOff is false for a Canadian card.

Mexico’s right holds only “siempre y cuando el Cliente no haya utilizado u operado los productos o servicios financieros contratados” (art. 11 Bis 1, read 2026-10-15 at diputados.gob.mx, last reform 14 November 2025); SLATE didn’t ask. SLATE can tell: usedSince counts a payment out of the account by its holder, a card’s purchase among them, and not the bank’s fees, its interest or its tax; money paid in isn’t counted, an account being funded to be opened (SLATE’s reading). A used Mexican account is out of its cooling-off.

A term’s interest taken during the term was found on canceling by its memo alone, “Interest: FestzinsSparen”, which every term at the bank shares, so canceling a new term took back what an older one had paid: out of the primary, off the year’s income, and counted in the refusal (€6.93 in the skeptic’s probe). bank.take_term_interest now carries the term itself in a posting of nothing, interestPaidSince finds a term’s payments by that posting, and the reversal leaves the zero posting out. Interest taken before the fix carries no such posting and isn’t found on canceling (in a save from before it, that interest gets no refusal and no reversal).

The cooling-off period ended at the hour the account opened on its last day (openedAt + days, or afterBusinessDays at the same hour), though Directive 2002/65/EC art. 6(1) gives 14 calendar days, SOR/2021-181 s.5(1) “within 14 business days after the day on which [it] is opened”, and LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1 “diez días hábiles posteriores”, and the panel named the day: an RBC account “until January 23” was refused at 11:30 AM on the 23rd. coolingOffEnds returns the last moment of that day in the save’s zone (endOfDay), and the panel names the date in that zone.
gapsOpen: unresolved: genuinely unreachable in a played life (the US has no cooling-off period in content/accountlife.ts, so inCoolingOff is false for every New Haven account). The New Haven half (no Cancel It, the refusal, the account kept) is proved; abroad the card branch (London), the current-account branch and its refusals are proved, the panel drawn while a refusal holds (the reason under it, Cancel It grayed with the same words), and three defects are fixed: a current account is settled on canceling as Close It settles one (its interest paid, its fees charged, in Canada its fees refunded), each part played abroad. From the later pass of 2026-10-15: canceling follows each country’s rule on interest (kept in Britain and Canada, returned in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico) and on charges (refunded for any deposit account in Canada and Mexico); Korea’s deposits have no cooling-off; and Close It refuses a German account its closing fees would overdraw, as Cancel It does. From that day’s recheck, five more defects fixed abroad: a term’s interest taken during the term is refused back out of a primary that doesn’t hold it (Berlin); Canada’s refund leaves out overdraft interest (Toronto); Canada’s 14 and Mexico’s 10 days are counted as business days, on the panel’s “until” date too (Toronto, Mexico City); Canada’s cards have no cooling-off (Toronto); a Mexican account once used has none (Mexico City). Mexico’s half of both rules and the German interest tax’s reversal are tested. From that day’s second recheck, two more defects fixed abroad: a term’s taken interest is found by the term itself, not by the name every term at the bank shares, so canceling a new Deutsche Bank term no longer takes back an older one’s (Berlin); and the period runs to the end of its last day, as each rule counts it, not to the hour the account opened (Toronto, Berlin). The refusal’s one-cent threshold is tested. Each FIXTURE, as no played life banks outside the US.
after.disposition: Still unreachable: the US has no cooling-off. Every closure the recheck claims is real, and its tests fail without the fixes, by the mutation record and by term2.ts rerun. Two new defects abroad were found and reproduced, so the row text's 'evidence complete abroad' overstates.

problems: interestPaidSince (accountlife.ts:170-172) matches a term's taken interest by memo alone: t.memo === `Interest: ${account.name}`. Every term at a bank has the same name, term.called (lending.ts, bank.open_term), and take_term_interest (:484) and maturity (:684) both post that memo. So canceling a new term reverses interest paid by an older term of the same product after the new one opened. It takes it back out of the primary, takes it off the year's income (recordInterest), and counts it in cancelRefusal's refusal. Probe (scratchpad/probe/term3.ts), Berlin, Deutsche Bank: term A of €10,000 opened; 10 days later term B of €10,000 opened; a day later A's €6.93 taken; B canceled. Result: 'Interest returned: FestzinsSparen, canceled' posts AktivKonto -693 and Interest +693. The primary ends €6.93 short of what it should hold, and A is still open with its interest gone. This is reachable abroad at every bank with interestDuringTerm.

The cooling-off ends at the opening moment's time of day on the last day: coolingOffEnds (accountlife.ts:272, :275) and afterBusinessDays (bankdays.ts:55-63) return openedAt shifted by whole days, and inCoolingOff tests sim.now <= ends. The panel says 'until <that date>' (BankAccountLife.tsx, formatDate(ends)), and both rules cover the whole last day: 'within 14 business days after the day on which ... opened' (SOR/2021-181 s.5(1)) and 'diez días hábiles posteriores'. Probe (scratchpad/probe/lastday.ts): Toronto, an RBC account opened 5 January at 7:30 AM; the panel says until January 23; at 11:30 AM on 23 January Cancel It is refused 'Its cooling-off period has passed'. Mexico City (Banorte) is the same: until January 19, refused at 11:30 AM on the 19th. The calendar-day countries do the same, as they did before. The Banorte test cancels at 9 AM on 10 February against a noon opening, so it never meets the boundary.
The threshold mutation the result marks 'not run' (`amount <= into.balance + 1`, accountlife.ts:251) survives: the Berlin term test tries only primary balances of 0 and exactly 6_30, never 6_29.
The guide's 'In Canada and Mexico the fees charged while it was open are refunded, but not overdraft interest' leaves out the machine owner's fee, which is also excluded (:206). This is minor.

From 2026-10-12 the link draws, for every payment, on easy-access savings at the bank of the current account the payment comes from: the primary for the day’s spending, the account a card’s autopay is set on for that autopay, and a loan’s repayment account for the loan; a change of primary leaves a card’s autopay and a loan’s repayment where they were. How You Pay lists each paying account and what it pays, and turning the link On is refused only where none has such savings. With Chase savings, a Citi loan repaid from Chase and Citi made primary, the link is offered, turned On, and pays the loan off from Chase savings (bank.repay_loan), and a card’s autopay left on Chase is paid from Chase savings through the clock where until then it bounced (defects-r3b-1.test.ts). Until then this row read ‘savings existence’, and said the card’s autopay reaching linked savings wasn’t checked. What isn’t: a loan’s monthly payment drawn from them by the clock (lending.test.ts sets the link by hand and doesn’t check which account paid; defects-r3b-1.test.ts pays the loan off by the command). The fourth review didn’t name this row; it was read while settling the rows it did.

review.claim: How You Pay sets everyday (debit, credit or cash) and linkSavings. On is refused unless some current account a payment comes from has easy-access savings at its own bank (linkCovers). Spending then goes on the chosen means (cash first, credit first, else debit). Linked savings covers what the current account can't for each payment, at that account's own bank: the day's spending from the primary, a card's autopay from its autopay account, and a loan's payments from its repayment account.

review.claim: Where the country has a switching service (SWITCHING), Switch schedules bank.switch_complete on the service's working days, or a later chosen working day, with a review the next working day and a cancel window. On the day, the new bank's accounts receive the balances, standing orders and scheduled payments are re-pointed, and so on. Where there's no service it's refused with the steps to take. Refused too for a ChexSystems report, collections, no photo ID, an overdraft, or a switch already under way.

review.claim: Move Money moves an amount between two of the holder's own current or easy-access savings accounts. It's refused past the balance, for the same account, from an account a switch left in debt, when dormant, past Germany's allowance, past room after the withdrawal fee, or when closing. At one bank it posts at once; between banks it goes out now and lands in the sending bank's days, held to its limits. Past the free withdrawals it charges the fee. It counts as a withdrawal, and its balance effect feeds the fee waivers (lowest/average) and the no-withdrawals bonus.

review.claim: A current account opens at another bank where you live, either at once or after the bank's review. The application is refused if you already keep an account there or one is under review, if you owe that bank a charged-off debt, if a ChexSystems report turns you away, without a photo ID in force, under the bank's minimum age, at Capital One or Citi for anyone not a US person, or in a branch you can't get to. findings.what: Credit score can be farmed by moving the card statement day forward each day: every move cancels the pending statement and schedules one from now, and a statement with nothing owed reports a month paid on time
findings.evidence: Measured with vite-node on a New York life (seed probe-sd), card at 0: 20 card.set_statement_day moves over 20 days fired 20 statements and moved the score from 640 to 700 (past the 670 loan line and the 700 raise line). The only test is cardlife.test.ts:169, which checks the next date.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow one move per cycle (or the next statement on the new day in the following month whenever it would fall less than about a month after the last one). Also make reportMonth/annual fee one per calendar month. Add a test that moving the day can't produce two statements in a month.

findings.what: Two statements in one month (from a statement-day move) charge the yearly fee twice in the anniversary month and leave two card.due items, which can each charge a late fee and add a missed payment (suspension comes at once)
findings.where: src/engine/systems/credit.ts:709 (month-only check, comment assumes one statement a month), :736 scheduleDue, :791-831
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code, not measured. set_statement_day cancels only STATEMENT_KIND items (cardlife.ts:161-164), never a pending DUE_KIND item
findings.suggestedFix: Cancel or merge the pending due when a new statement supersedes it, and key the yearly fee on a stored lastAnnualFeeAt

findings.what: Cancelling a new savings account in its cooling-off period (and escheat closing one) leaves standing orders and scheduled payments pointing at the closed account
findings.evidence: Measured (Toronto, TD): after bank.cancel_new the order is still listed 95 days later and fails monthly with 'TD ePremium Savings is closed'. The scheduled payment ended 'done' with no notice and no posting.
findings.suggestedFix: Move closeSavings' order/payment clean-up into a shared helper and call it from cancel_new and idleAccounts. Have the scheduled payment notify when an account is closed.

findings.what: A US card's autopay that bounces is charged both the returned-payment fee and the late fee for the same missed due date. Reg Z §1026.52(b)(2)(ii) allows one penalty fee per event, and the code follows Reg Z's other limits (§1026.52(a), (b)(2)(i)(B), safe harbor)
findings.evidence: Both postings run in the same DUE handler when asked > autopayReach and paid < due; cardlife.test.ts:299 asserts only the returned fee
findings.suggestedFix: For iso US, skip the late fee when the returned-payment fee was charged for this due, or charge the larger of the two

findings.what: Card hardship plan is granted on request with no test of hardship: it freezes all interest, the payment is a 48th of the balance, and paying it counts as on time (score +), with no mark on the record
findings.evidence: No condition beyond owed>0, and the button shows whenever something is owed (BankCard.tsx:237)
findings.suggestedFix: Gate on missed payments or a fall in income, and/or report the plan (a mark or a hold on score gains)

findings.what: 'Left To Spend' on the card panel is limit minus owed. It ignores what the engine actually lets onto the card (suspension, closing, lock or stop, payment holds, the over-limit opt-in), so a suspended or locked card can show room to spend
findings.suggestedFix: Show cardRoom(person, card), and say why when it is 0

findings.what: Fraud on a card with a large-payment alert sends two 'A Large Payment' notices with different bodies, so the dedupe doesn't merge them
findings.evidence: Code reading; sim.notify merges only identical title+body (simulation.ts:716)
findings.suggestedFix: Skip category 'card-fraud' in the alerts sweep, or drop the notify in somebodyElse

findings.what: Unauthorized card charges earn rewards: NOT_PURCHASES doesn't include 'card-fraud', and the refund never takes the reward back
bank.new_number only costs something (the debit card is stopped until a replacement comes). No compromise state exists, so it changes no later outcome
findings.evidence: fraudOn draws on rng and card state alone
findings.suggestedFix: Either model a compromised number that raises fraud odds until renumbered, or say on screen that it's cosmetic

findings.what: statementAfter takes the first pending card.statement in the universe, not this person's or card's. With several cards, learnedAt can come from another card's date
Card statement periods are all cut on today's statement day. After a move, past statements no longer match the dates they were issued on
findings.suggestedFix: Derive the period bounds from the statements that actually happened (done STATEMENT_KIND items)
